---
title: "Survey-to-FG Density Pipeline: Methodology"
subtitle: "Generalized functions applied to MEDITS (Western Mediterranean), with both GSA-based and custom-region examples"
author: "Daniel Vilas"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    number-sections: true
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
    theme: cosmo
params:
  ## Inputs of the pipeline run done by this document. Change a value and
  ## click Render: the pipeline reruns with these values and the HTML shows
  ## the new plots and tables. Values are R expressions.
  model_gsas: "1:11"              # GSAs of the model area, e.g. "c(6, 7)"
  model_area_basis: "whole_gsa"   # "whole_gsa" or "medits_10_800"
  year_ecopath: "1994:1996"       # Ecopath baseline years
  ts_years: "1995:2023"           # Ecosim biomass years
  start_year: 1994                # first catch/effort year
  end_year: 2023                  # last catch/effort year
  ## What the render reruns before building the HTML:
  ##   "all"        - the whole pipeline 01 -> 05 with the inputs above
  ##                  (about 10 min; the first run after a change needs internet)
  ##   "validation" - only 05_validation.R (redraws the validation plots)
  ##   "none"       - nothing; uses the outputs already on disk
  regenerate: "none"
server: shiny
execute:
  eval: false
  echo: true
  freeze: false   # overrides the site's freeze: auto for THIS document specifically -
                   # this doc's setup chunk copies PNGs from an external out_dir/plots
                   # folder that changes independently of the .qmd's own source code,
                   # which is exactly the case freeze:auto can't detect (it only checks
                   # whether the .qmd's OWN code changed, not files it reads at render
                   # time) - so this doc always re-executes fully, every render
---

```{r}
#| label: setup-copy-figures
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| include: false

## Copies figures from each script's absolute, machine-local out_dir into
## a local "figures/" folder next to this .qmd, so relative image paths
## still resolve once rendered and deployed elsewhere (e.g. GitHub Pages).
## Always overwrites, so a stale copy never lingers after the real plot changes.
## Path resolution works without RStudio (e.g. `quarto preview` / `quarto
## render` from a terminal). Order for each path:
##   git_dir: env var WMED_GIT_DIR > the repo this .qmd sits in (the .qmd
##            lives in <git_dir>/scripts/, and knitr runs in that folder)
##            > daniel's path > RStudio picker.
##   out_dir: env var WMED_OUT_DIR > first line of qmd_out_dir.txt next to
##            this .qmd (machine-specific, git-ignored) > a literal out_dir
##            in 01_biomass.R that exists on this machine > RStudio picker
##            > none (figures/downloads are then skipped with a placeholder,
##            the render does not stop).
.env_dir <- function(var) { v <- Sys.getenv(var, ""); if (nzchar(v) && dir.exists(path.expand(v))) path.expand(v) else NA_character_ }

git_dir <- .env_dir("WMED_GIT_DIR")
if (is.na(git_dir) && file.exists(file.path("..", "scripts", "01_biomass.R"))) git_dir <- normalizePath("..")
if (is.na(git_dir) && file.exists(file.path("01_biomass.R"))) git_dir <- normalizePath("..")
if (is.na(git_dir) && dir.exists("/Users/daniel/Documents/GitHub/WMed_EwE/")) git_dir <- "/Users/daniel/Documents/GitHub/WMed_EwE/"
if (is.na(git_dir) && requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE) && rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
  sel <- rstudioapi::selectDirectory(caption = "Select the WMed_EwE repository (git_dir)")
  if (!is.null(sel) && dir.exists(sel)) git_dir <- sel
}
if (is.na(git_dir)) stop("Cannot find the WMed_EwE repository: render this .qmd from <git_dir>/scripts/ or set the environment variable WMED_GIT_DIR.")
message("git_dir (resolved): ", git_dir)

## --- Regenerate the pipeline outputs before copying them (params$regenerate) ---
## Runs run_pipeline_demo.R in a SEPARATE R process (Rscript), so the
## pipeline's own clean start cannot touch this document's objects; paths
## come from config.R as for a normal run. The full log of each script is
## in out_dir as usual; a failed step stops the render with its message.
.regen <- if (exists("params") && !is.null(params$regenerate)) params$regenerate else "none"
if (!identical(.regen, "none")) {
  .steps <- switch(.regen, validation = "5", all = "1:5",
                   stop("params$regenerate must be \"none\", \"validation\" or \"all\" (got \"", .regen, "\")."))
  .demo <- file.path(git_dir, "scripts", "run_pipeline_demo.R")
  message("Regenerating pipeline outputs (", .regen, ", steps ", .steps, ") with ", .demo, " ...")
  .old_wd <- setwd(file.path(git_dir, "scripts"))
  .p <- function(x, default) if (!is.null(params[[x]])) as.character(params[[x]]) else default
  .code <- paste0("CLEAN_START <- FALSE; RUN_STEPS <- ", .steps,
                  "; MODEL_GSAS <- ", .p("model_gsas", "1:11"),
                  "; MODEL_AREA_BASIS <- '", .p("model_area_basis", "whole_gsa"), "'",
                  "; YEAR_ECOPATH <- ", .p("year_ecopath", "1994:1996"),
                  "; TS_YEARS <- ", .p("ts_years", "1995:2023"),
                  "; START_YEAR <- ", .p("start_year", "1994"),
                  "; END_YEAR <- ", .p("end_year", "2023"),
                  "; source('run_pipeline_demo.R')")
  message("Pipeline call: ", .code)
  .status <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c("-e", shQuote(.code)))
  setwd(.old_wd)
  if (!identical(.status, 0L)) stop("run_pipeline_demo.R failed (exit status ", .status, ") - see the logs in out_dir.")
  message("Pipeline outputs regenerated.")
}

extract_out_dir <- function(script_path, script_label) {
  d <- .env_dir("WMED_OUT_DIR")
  if (!is.na(d)) return(d)
  if (file.exists("qmd_out_dir.txt")) {
    p <- path.expand(trimws(readLines("qmd_out_dir.txt", warn = FALSE)[1]))
    if (nzchar(p) && dir.exists(p)) return(p)
    warning("qmd_out_dir.txt points to '", p, "', which does not exist on this machine.")
  }
  if (file.exists(script_path)) {
    lits <- gsub('.*out_dir\\s*<-\\s*"([^"]+)".*', '\\1', grep('out_dir\\s*<-\\s*"', readLines(script_path, warn = FALSE), value = TRUE))
    lits <- lits[dir.exists(lits)]
    if (length(lits)) return(lits[1])
  }
  if (requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE) && rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
    sel <- rstudioapi::selectDirectory(caption = paste("Select the output directory", script_label, "wrote to"))
    if (!is.null(sel) && dir.exists(sel)) return(sel)
  }
  warning("No out_dir found for ", script_label, " - set WMED_OUT_DIR or write the path in qmd_out_dir.txt",
          " next to this .qmd. Figures/downloads are skipped.")
  NA_character_
}

biomass_script_path <- file.path(git_dir, "scripts", "01_biomass.R")
gsa_out_dir <- extract_out_dir(biomass_script_path, "01_biomass.R")
if (!exists("CUSTOM_AREA_NAME")) CUSTOM_AREA_NAME <- "custom_region"
custom_out_dir <- if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, CUSTOM_AREA_NAME) else NA_character_
gsa_plots_dir <- if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, "plots", "biomass") else NA_character_
custom_plots_dir <- if (!is.na(custom_out_dir)) file.path(custom_out_dir, "plots") else NA_character_
message("GSA plots directory (resolved): ", gsa_plots_dir)
message("Custom-region plots directory (resolved): ", custom_plots_dir)

## Relative to this .qmd (unlike out_dir), so it's committed/pushed with it.
local_figures_dir <- "figures"
if (!dir.exists(local_figures_dir)) dir.create(local_figures_dir)

## Copies a list of figures (src dir, src file, local name); always
## overwrites so a stale copy never lingers.
copy_figures <- function(items) {
  for (p in items) {
    if (is.na(p$dir)) next   # out_dir couldn't be auto-detected - already warned above
    src <- file.path(p$dir, p$file)
    dst <- file.path(local_figures_dir, p$dst)
    if (file.exists(src)) file.copy(src, dst, overwrite = TRUE) else
      warning("Plot not found at ", src, " - run the relevant pipeline script first.")
  }
}
cr <- paste0("_", CUSTOM_AREA_NAME)
copy_figures(list(
  list(dir = gsa_plots_dir, file = "survey_sample_coverage_map.png", dst = "survey_sample_coverage_map.png"),
  list(dir = gsa_plots_dir, file = "survey_sample_coverage_map_by_year.png", dst = "survey_sample_coverage_map_by_year.png"),
  list(dir = gsa_plots_dir, file = "survey_fg_density_timeseries.png", dst = "survey_fg_density_timeseries.png"),
  list(dir = gsa_plots_dir, file = "survey_fg_density_timeseries_regional.png", dst = "survey_fg_density_timeseries_regional.png"),
  list(dir = gsa_plots_dir, file = "survey_fg_depth_strata_profile.png", dst = "survey_fg_depth_strata_profile.png"),
  list(dir = custom_plots_dir, file = paste0("survey_sample_coverage_map", cr, ".png"), dst = "custom_survey_sample_coverage_map.png"),
  list(dir = custom_plots_dir, file = paste0("survey_fg_density_timeseries", cr, ".png"), dst = "custom_survey_fg_density_timeseries.png")
))

## The other pipeline scripts (02-05) share the same out_dir.
pipeline_out_dir <- gsa_out_dir
pd <- function(...) if (!is.na(pipeline_out_dir)) file.path(pipeline_out_dir, "plots", ...) else NA_character_
message("Pipeline plots directory (resolved): ", pd())
copy_figures(list(
  list(dir = pd("biomass"),    file = "biomass_by_fg_source.png", dst = "biomass_by_fg_source.png"),
  list(dir = pd("biomass"),    file = "survey_fg_density_timeseries_regional.png", dst = "biomass_survey_fg_density_timeseries_regional.png"),
  list(dir = pd("fisheries"),  file = "07_catch_by_fg_and_fleet.png", dst = "07_catch_by_fg_and_fleet.png"),
  list(dir = pd("fisheries"),  file = "08_discards_by_fg_and_fleet.png", dst = "08_discards_by_fg_and_fleet.png"),
  list(dir = pd("fisheries"),  file = "01_catches_per_FG.png", dst = "pipeline_01_catches_per_FG.png"),
  list(dir = pd("fisheries"),  file = "05_effort_by_country_fleet.png", dst = "05_effort_by_country_fleet.png"),
  list(dir = pd("validation"), file = "fg_pb_qb_scatter.png", dst = "fg_pb_qb_scatter.png"),
  list(dir = pd("validation"), file = "F_by_fg.png", dst = "F_by_fg.png"),
  list(dir = pd("validation"), file = "PQ_ratio_by_fg.png", dst = "PQ_ratio_by_fg.png"),
  list(dir = pd("validation"), file = "biomass_vs_old_model_by_fg.png", dst = "biomass_vs_old_model_by_fg.png"),
  list(dir = pd("validation"), file = "11_zooplankton_total_field_check.png", dst = "11_zooplankton_total_field_check.png"),
  list(dir = pd("diets"),      file = "diet_matrix_heatmap.png", dst = "diet_matrix_heatmap.png")
))

## Wraps knitr::include_graphics() with an existence check, so a figure
## whose source script hasn't run yet shows a placeholder instead of
## hard-failing the entire render.
safe_include_graphics <- function(path, script_hint) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    knitr::include_graphics(path)
  } else {
    knitr::asis_output(paste0(
      "> **Figure not yet available** - `", path, "` doesn't exist yet. Run `",
      script_hint, "` first, then re-render this document.\n"
    ))
  }
}

## Same copy pattern as the figures above, but for the actual data outputs
## (ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx and CSVs), so a reader of the rendered HTML
## can download the real generated files directly.
local_downloads_dir <- "downloads"
if (!dir.exists(local_downloads_dir)) dir.create(local_downloads_dir)

files_needed <- list(
  list(dir = gsa_out_dir, file = "ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx", dst = "ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx"),
  list(dir = if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, "biomass") else NA_character_, file = "survey_fg_annual_index.csv", dst = "survey_fg_annual_index.csv"),
  list(dir = if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, "biomass") else NA_character_, file = "survey_fg_annual_index_regional_combined.csv", dst = "survey_fg_annual_index_regional_combined.csv"),
  list(dir = if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, "biomass") else NA_character_, file = "survey_unmatched_for_manual_review.csv", dst = "survey_unmatched_for_manual_review.csv"),
  list(dir = if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, "biomass") else NA_character_, file = "survey_outliers_flagged.csv", dst = "survey_outliers_flagged.csv"),
  list(dir = if (!is.na(gsa_out_dir)) file.path(gsa_out_dir, "biomass") else NA_character_, file = "strata_area_by_area.csv", dst = "strata_area_by_area.csv"),
  list(dir = custom_out_dir, file = "ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx", dst = "custom_ecopath_ecosim_inputs.xlsx"),
  list(dir = custom_out_dir, file = paste0("survey_fg_annual_index", cr, ".csv"), dst = "custom_survey_fg_annual_index.csv"),
  list(dir = custom_out_dir, file = paste0("survey_fg_annual_index_regional", cr, ".csv"), dst = "custom_survey_fg_annual_index_regional.csv"),
  list(dir = custom_out_dir, file = paste0("survey_unmatched_for_manual_review", cr, ".csv"), dst = "custom_survey_unmatched_for_manual_review.csv"),
  list(dir = custom_out_dir, file = paste0("survey_outliers_flagged", cr, ".csv"), dst = "custom_survey_outliers_flagged.csv"),
  list(dir = custom_out_dir, file = "strata_area_by_area.csv", dst = "custom_strata_area_by_area.csv")
)
for (p in files_needed) {
  if (is.na(p$dir)) next   # out_dir couldn't be auto-detected - already warned above
  src <- file.path(p$dir, p$file)
  dst <- file.path(local_downloads_dir, p$dst)
  if (file.exists(src)) file.copy(src, dst, overwrite = TRUE) else
    warning("Output file not found at ", src, " - run 01_biomass.R first.")
}

## Renders a real download link if the file was copied above, or a
## placeholder (like safe_include_graphics()) if it hasn't been produced yet.
safe_download_link <- function(local_path, label, script_hint) {
  if (file.exists(local_path)) {
    size_kb <- round(file.info(local_path)$size / 1024, 1)
    knitr::asis_output(paste0(
      "[", label, "](", local_path, "){download} (", size_kb, " KB)\n\n"
    ))
  } else {
    knitr::asis_output(paste0(
      "> **Not yet available** - `", local_path, "` doesn't exist yet. Run `",
      script_hint, "` first, then re-render this document.\n\n"
    ))
  }
}
```

## Configure and run the pipeline {#sec-configure}

Pick the model area on the map, set the years and options, and click **Run pipeline**. The run (01 → 05) goes in the background with exactly the settings shown in the *Settings block* box; when it finishes, the plots at the bottom and the tables in the output folder are updated. A full run takes about 10 minutes (the first run after a change of GSAs needs internet for the bathymetry). The same settings block can be copied or downloaded to run the pipeline from the R console instead.

This works when the document is opened with **Run Document** in RStudio (or `quarto serve medbs_pipeline_methodology.qmd` in a terminal). A plain HTML file opened from disk shows the page but cannot run R.

```{r}
#| label: run-ui
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
library(shiny)
## GFCM GSA polygons (official GFCM_GSA.zip, simplified to 5 % of the
## vertices for display; GSA 11 has two polygons, W and E Sardinia).
.gsa_geojson <- if (file.exists("gsa_boundaries_westmed.geojson"))
  paste(readLines("gsa_boundaries_westmed.geojson", warn = FALSE), collapse = "") else "null"
.gsa_names <- c("Northern Alboran", "Alboran Island", "Southern Alboran", "Algeria", "Balearic Islands",
                "Northern Spain", "Gulf of Lion", "Corsica", "Ligurian & N Tyrrhenian", "S & C Tyrrhenian", "Sardinia")
.card <- function(step, title, icon, ..., class = "") {
  tags$div(class = paste("card wm-card mb-3", class),
           tags$div(class = "card-header wm-card-header",
                    tags$span(class = "wm-step", step), tags$span(class = "wm-icon", icon), title),
           tags$div(class = "card-body", ...))
}
.switch <- function(id, label, help, value = TRUE) {
  tags$div(class = "form-check form-switch wm-switch",
           tags$input(class = "form-check-input", type = "checkbox", role = "switch", id = id,
                      checked = if (value) NA else NULL),
           tags$label(class = "form-check-label", `for` = id, label),
           tags$div(class = "wm-help", help))
}

  .card("1", "Model area", "\U0001F5FA",

            tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary", `data-gsas` = "1,2,5,6,7,8,9,10,11", "MEDITS GSAs"),
            tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary", `data-gsas` = "1,2,5,6", "Spain"),
            tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary", `data-gsas` = "7,8", "France"),
            tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary", `data-gsas` = "9,10,11", "Italy"),
            tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger", `data-gsas` = "", "Clear")),
          tags$div(class = "wm-gsa-grid",
            checkboxGroupInput("gsas", NULL, choices = setNames(1:11, paste0(1:11, " - ", .gsa_names)), selected = 1:11)),
          radioButtons("basis", "Area basis (A_model)",
                       choices = c("Whole GSA, coast to bottom" = "whole_gsa", "MEDITS strata 10-800 m only" = "medits_10_800"),
                       selected = "whole_gsa"),
          tags$div(class = "wm-help", "Every t/km\u00b2 is per km\u00b2 of this area. Whole GSA: depths outside 10-800 m filled with AquaMaps.")),
        conditionalPanel("input.area_mode == 'custom'",
          textInput("area_name", "Area name (AREA_NAME)", "custom_region"),
          tags$div(class = "wm-help", "Used for the output subfolder, so runs for different regions do not overwrite each other."),
          fluidRow(column(6, numericInput("bbox_xmin", "Lon min", 2, step = 0.1)), column(6, numericInput("bbox_xmax", "Lon max", 8, step = 0.1))),
          fluidRow(column(6, numericInput("bbox_ymin", "Lat min", 38, step = 0.1)), column(6, numericInput("bbox_ymax", "Lat max", 42, step = 0.1))),
          tags$div(class = "alert alert-warning py-2 small",
                   "A custom box runs 01_biomass.R only (02-05 work on GSAs). Use the settings block below; the Run button is for GSA runs.")))),
    tags$hr(),
    uiOutput("area_summary")),

  ## 2. Years and options --------------------------------------------------
  fluidRow(
    column(6, .card("2", "Years", "\U0001F4C5",
      sliderInput("ecopath_years", "Ecopath baseline (YEAR_ECOPATH)", min = 1990, max = 2023, value = c(1994, 1996), step = 1, sep = "", width = "100%"),
      sliderInput("ts_years", "Ecosim biomass series (TS_YEARS)", min = 1990, max = 2023, value = c(1995, 2023), step = 1, sep = "", width = "100%"),
      sliderInput("catch_years", "Catch and effort series (START_YEAR - END_YEAR)", min = 1990, max = 2023, value = c(1994, 2023), step = 1, sep = "", width = "100%"))),
    column(6, .card("3", "Options", "\u2699\ufe0f",
      .switch("strata", "Strata-weighted density (STRATA)", "Off = simple mean density instead of the depth-stratum (area-weighted) estimator.", TRUE),
      .switch("drop_outliers", "Remove flagged outlier hauls (DROP_OUTLIERS)", "Off = outliers are only reported in survey_outliers_flagged.csv.", TRUE),
      .switch("normalize_ts", "Ecosim series as relative index (NORMALIZE_TS)", "Off = raw density (t/km\u00b2) instead of first value = 1.", TRUE),
      radioButtons("steps", "Scripts to run", inline = TRUE,
                   choices = c("All 01-05" = "1:5", "02-05 (keep biomass)" = "2:5", "Only 05 validation" = "5"), selected = "1:5")))),

  ## 4. Run ----------------------------------------------------------------
  .card("4", "Run", "\u25B6\ufe0f",
    fluidRow(
      column(5,
        actionButton("run", "Run pipeline", class = "btn-primary", icon = icon("play")),
        tags$p(),
        uiOutput("run_progress"),
        verbatimTextOutput("run_status")),
      column(7,
        tags$div(class = "d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-1",
          tags$strong("Settings block"),
          tags$div(
            tags$button(type = "button", id = "wm-copy", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary", "Copy"),
            downloadButton("dl_config", "Download .R", class = "btn-sm btn-outline-secondary"))),
        textOutput("config_text", container = function(...) tags$pre(class = "wm-config", ...))))),

  ## Results ---------------------------------------------------------------
  .card("5", "Results", "\U0001F4CA", tags$div(class = "wm-results", uiOutput("results"))),

  tags$script(type = "application/json", id = "wm-gsa-geojson", HTML(.gsa_geojson)),
  tags$script(HTML(r"---(
(function () {
  var UNSURVEYED = [3, 4];
  function checked() {
    return $('input[name="gsas"]:checked').map(function () { return +this.value; }).get();
  }
  function setGsas(list) {
    var boxes = $('input[name="gsas"]');
    boxes.each(function () { $(this).prop('checked', list.indexOf(+this.value) !== -1); });
    boxes.first().trigger('change');
  }
  function init() {
    if (typeof L === 'undefined' || !document.getElementById('wm-map')) { return setTimeout(init, 200); }
    var map = L.map('wm-map', { scrollWheelZoom: false, zoomSnap: 0.25 });
    // Esri Ocean basemap (no API key); falls back to OpenStreetMap if its tiles fail
    var base = L.tileLayer('https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Ocean/World_Ocean_Base/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}', {
      attribution: 'Tiles &copy; Esri - GEBCO, NOAA, Garmin', maxZoom: 10 }).addTo(map);
    var fails = 0;
    base.on('tileerror', function () {
      if (++fails === 3) {
        map.removeLayer(base);
        L.tileLayer('https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png', {
          attribution: '&copy; OpenStreetMap contributors', maxZoom: 10 }).addTo(map);
      }
    });
    var data = null;
    try { data = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('wm-gsa-geojson').textContent); } catch (e) {}
    var layer = null, rect = null;
    function style(f) {
      var g = f.properties.gsa_num, on = checked().indexOf(g) !== -1, uns = UNSURVEYED.indexOf(g) !== -1;
      return { color: on ? '#0b4f6c' : '#8a99a6', weight: on ? 1.5 : 1,
               fillColor: on ? (uns ? '#f0a202' : '#1b7f9e') : '#d5dde3', fillOpacity: on ? 0.5 : 0.15 };
    }
    if (data) {
      layer = L.geoJSON(data, {
        style: style,
        onEachFeature: function (f, l) {
          var g = f.properties.gsa_num;
          l.bindTooltip('GSA ' + g + ' - ' + f.properties.SMU_NAME +
                        (UNSURVEYED.indexOf(g) !== -1 ? ' (no MEDITS)' : ''), { sticky: true });
          l.on('click', function () {
            if ($('input[name="area_mode"]:checked').val() !== 'westmed') return;
            var s = checked(), i = s.indexOf(g);
            if (i === -1) s.push(g); else s.splice(i, 1);
            setGsas(s);
          });
          l.on('mouseover', function () { l.setStyle({ weight: 3 }); });
          l.on('mouseout', function () { layer.resetStyle(l); });
        }
      }).addTo(map);
      map.fitBounds(layer.getBounds(), { padding: [10, 10] });
      var legend = L.control({ position: 'topright' });
      legend.onAdd = function () {
        var d = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'wm-legend');
        d.innerHTML = '<i style="background:#1b7f9e"></i>In the model, MEDITS survey<br>' +
                      '<i style="background:#f0a202"></i>In the model, no survey (GSA 3, 4)<br>' +
                      '<i style="background:#d5dde3"></i>Not in the model';
        return d;
      };
      legend.addTo(map);
    } else { map.setView([39, 5], 5); }
    function drawBox() {
      if (rect) { map.removeLayer(rect); rect = null; }
      var custom = $('input[name="area_mode"]:checked').val() === 'custom';
      if (layer) layer.setStyle(custom ? { fillOpacity: 0.05, color: '#b8c4cc', weight: 1 } : style);
      if (!custom) { if (layer) layer.setStyle(style); return; }
      var v = ['bbox_xmin', 'bbox_xmax', 'bbox_ymin', 'bbox_ymax'].map(function (id) { return parseFloat($('#' + id).val()); });
      if (v.every(function (x) { return !isNaN(x); }) && v[1] > v[0] && v[3] > v[2]) {
        rect = L.rectangle([[v[2], v[0]], [v[3], v[1]]], { color: '#d9480f', weight: 2, fillOpacity: 0.15 }).addTo(map);
      }
    }
    $(document).on('change', 'input[name="gsas"]', function () { if (layer) layer.setStyle(style); });
    $(document).on('change', 'input[name="area_mode"]', drawBox);
    $(document).on('input change', '#bbox_xmin, #bbox_xmax, #bbox_ymin, #bbox_ymax', drawBox);
    $(document).on('click', '.wm-quick .btn', function () {
      var s = String($(this).data('gsas'));
      setGsas(s ? s.split(',').map(Number) : []);
    });
    $(document).on('click', '#wm-copy', function () {
      var btn = this;
      navigator.clipboard.writeText($('#config_text').text()).then(function () {
        btn.textContent = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(function () { btn.textContent = 'Copy'; }, 1200);
      });
    });
    setTimeout(function () { map.invalidateSize(); if (layer) map.fitBounds(layer.getBounds(), { padding: [10, 10] }); }, 400);
  }
  $(init);

  // --- Zoomable plot viewer: click a plot, wheel or +/- to zoom, drag to move, Esc to close
  var lb, img, sc = 1, tx = 0, ty = 0, drag = null;
  function apply() { img.style.transform = 'translate(' + tx + 'px,' + ty + 'px) scale(' + sc + ')'; }
  function fit() {
    var w = img.naturalWidth, h = img.naturalHeight, W = window.innerWidth, H = window.innerHeight;
    sc = Math.min(W / w, (H - 60) / h, 1); tx = (W - w * sc) / 2; ty = (H - h * sc) / 2 + 20; apply();
  }
  function zoomAt(f, cx, cy) {
    var ns = Math.min(Math.max(sc * f, 0.1), 8);
    tx = cx - (cx - tx) * ns / sc; ty = cy - (cy - ty) * ns / sc; sc = ns; apply();
  }
  function build() {
    lb = $('<div id="wm-lightbox"><div class="wm-lb-bar">' +
           '<button data-z="in">+</button><button data-z="out">&minus;</button>' +
           '<button data-z="fit">Fit</button><button data-z="full">100%</button><button data-z="close">Close &times;</button></div>' +
           '<img alt=""><div class="wm-lb-hint">Mouse wheel or +/- to zoom - drag to move - Esc to close</div></div>').appendTo('body');
    img = lb.find('img')[0];
    lb.on('click', 'button', function () {
      var z = $(this).data('z'), W = window.innerWidth / 2, H = window.innerHeight / 2;
      if (z === 'in') zoomAt(1.4, W, H); else if (z === 'out') zoomAt(1 / 1.4, W, H);
      else if (z === 'fit') fit(); else if (z === 'full') zoomAt(1 / sc, W, H); else lb.hide();
    });
    lb[0].addEventListener('wheel', function (e) { e.preventDefault(); zoomAt(e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.15 : 1 / 1.15, e.clientX, e.clientY); }, { passive: false });
    $(img).on('mousedown', function (e) { e.preventDefault(); drag = { x: e.clientX - tx, y: e.clientY - ty }; img.style.cursor = 'grabbing'; });
    $(document).on('mousemove', function (e) { if (drag) { tx = e.clientX - drag.x; ty = e.clientY - drag.y; apply(); } });
    $(document).on('mouseup', function () { drag = null; if (img) img.style.cursor = 'grab'; });
    $(document).on('keydown', function (e) { if (e.key === 'Escape') lb.hide(); });
  }
  function wmFilter() {
    var f = $('.wm-filter .btn.active').data('folder') || '', q = ($('#wm-search').val() || '').toLowerCase();
    $('.wm-thumb').each(function () {
      var ok = (!f || $(this).data('folder') === f) && (!q || String($(this).data('name')).indexOf(q) !== -1);
      $(this).toggle(ok);
    });
  }
  $(document).on('click', '.wm-filter .btn', function () {
    $('.wm-filter .btn').removeClass('active'); $(this).addClass('active'); wmFilter();
  });
  $(document).on('input', '#wm-search', wmFilter);
  $(document).on('click', '.wm-results img', function () {
    if (!this.src || this.naturalWidth === 0) return;
    if (!lb) build();
    img.onload = fit; img.src = this.src; lb.show();
    if (img.complete) fit();
  });
})();
)---"))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: run-server
#| context: server
#| eval: true
## Paths: this .qmd sits in <git_dir>/scripts; out_dir comes from config.R
## (the same file run_pipeline_demo.R reads).
.git_dir <- if (file.exists(file.path("..", "scripts", "01_biomass.R"))) normalizePath("..") else
  Sys.getenv("WMED_GIT_DIR", "/Users/daniel/Documents/GitHub/WMed_EwE")
.cfg <- new.env()
for (f in c(file.path(.git_dir, "config.R"), file.path(.git_dir, "scripts", "config.R")))
  if (file.exists(f)) { sys.source(f, envir = .cfg); break }
.out_dir <- if (exists("out_dir", envir = .cfg)) path.expand(get("out_dir", envir = .cfg)) else Sys.getenv("WMED_OUT_DIR", NA_character_)
## Run files live in out_dir/.qmd_run (not in R's temporary folder), so a page
## reopened later still knows the last run started from here, and a run
## that is still going.
.run_dir <- if (!is.na(.out_dir) && dir.exists(.out_dir)) file.path(.out_dir, ".qmd_run") else file.path(tempdir(), "wmed_qmd_run")
dir.create(.run_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
.status_file <- file.path(.run_dir, "status.txt")       # "done" or "error: ..." when the run ends; its time = end
.console <- file.path(.run_dir, "console.txt")          # everything the run prints
.progress_file <- file.path(.run_dir, "progress.txt")   # "--- Step i/5 ..." lines
.pid_file <- file.path(.run_dir, "pid.txt")             # process id of the run
.settings_file <- file.path(.run_dir, "settings.R")     # settings block of the run; its time = start

## Whole-GSA area of each GSA from the map polygons (km2). An approximate
## preview only: 01 computes the real A_model from the GSA shapefile and
## the bathymetry (795,431 km2 for GSAs 1-11 in the 2026-10-15 run; the
## simplified polygons give about 1 % more).
.gsa_km2 <- tryCatch({
  g <- sf::st_read(file.path(.git_dir, "scripts", "gsa_boundaries_westmed.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
  a <- tapply(as.numeric(sf::st_area(g)) / 1e6, g$gsa_num, sum)
  setNames(as.numeric(a), names(a))
}, error = function(e) NULL)
## Depth cells of the model area written by 01 (out_dir/biomass/
## model_area_cells.csv: GSA x depth band, km2, from the NOAA bathymetry).
## With whole_gsa it holds every depth band, so both bases can be summed
## from it: 10-800 m = cells with Depth_min_m >= 10 and Depth_max_m <= 800.
model_cells <- reactive({
  last_finished()
  f <- if (!is.na(.out_dir)) file.path(.out_dir, "biomass", "model_area_cells.csv") else ""
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  x <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(f), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(x) || !all(c("AreaID", "Depth_min_m", "Depth_max_m", "area_km2") %in% names(x))) NULL else x
})
## Coastal state of each GSA - the same table as GSA_COASTAL_STATE in 02_fisheries.R
.gsa_state <- c("1" = "Spain", "2" = "Spain", "3" = "Morocco", "4" = "Algeria", "5" = "Spain", "6" = "Spain",
                "7" = "France", "8" = "France", "9" = "Italy", "10" = "Italy", "11" = "Italy")
.unsurveyed <- c(3, 4)
## Expected minutes per script (01..05), from the 2026-10-15 run; 01 is much
## slower the first time after a change of GSAs (bathymetry download).
.step_min <- c(1.1, 1.5, 5.2, 1.2, 0.8)
.step_names <- c("01 biomass", "02 fisheries", "03 P/B, Q/B", "04 diets", "05 validation")

## --- Area summary cards ---------------------------------------------------
output$area_summary <- renderUI({
  stat <- function(label, value, note = NULL, warn = FALSE)
    column(3, tags$div(class = paste("wm-stat", if (warn) "warn"),
                       tags$div(class = "l", label), tags$div(class = "v", value),
                       if (!is.null(note)) tags$div(class = "n", note)))
  if (identical(input$area_mode, "custom")) {
    b <- c(input$bbox_xmin, input$bbox_xmax, input$bbox_ymin, input$bbox_ymax)
    ok <- all(is.finite(b)) && b[2] > b[1] && b[4] > b[3]
    km2 <- if (ok) (b[2] - b[1]) * 111.32 * cos(mean(b[3:4]) * pi / 180) * (b[4] - b[3]) * 110.57 else NA
    return(fluidRow(
      stat("Region", input$area_name),
      stat("Box", if (ok) sprintf("%.1f-%.1f\u00b0E, %.1f-%.1f\u00b0N", b[1], b[2], b[3], b[4]) else "invalid", warn = !ok),
      stat("Box area", if (ok) paste(format(round(km2, -2), big.mark = ","), "km\u00b2") else "-", "rectangle, land included"),
      stat("Scripts", "01 only", "02-05 need GSAs", warn = TRUE)))
  }
  g <- as.numeric(input$gsas)
  if (!length(g)) return(tags$div(class = "alert alert-danger mb-0", "No GSA selected - click the map or a quick-select button."))
  ## Area: from the depth cells 01 wrote (exact, from the bathymetry) when
  ## the last run covered these GSAs; otherwise the map polygons (whole GSA)
  cells <- model_cells()
  basis <- input$basis
  per_gsa <- if (!is.null(cells)) {
    keep <- if (identical(basis, "medits_10_800")) cells$Depth_min_m >= 10 & cells$Depth_max_m <= 800 else rep(TRUE, nrow(cells))
    tapply(cells$area_km2[keep], cells$AreaID[keep], sum)
  } else NULL
  have <- !is.null(per_gsa) && all(as.character(g) %in% names(per_gsa))
  fmt <- function(x) paste(format(round(x, -2), big.mark = ","), "km\u00b2")
  area_box <- if (have) {
    stat("Model area", fmt(sum(per_gsa[as.character(g)])),
         if (identical(basis, "medits_10_800")) "MEDITS strata 10-800 m, from the bathymetry (01)" else "whole GSA, coast to bottom (01)")
  } else if (identical(basis, "whole_gsa") && !is.null(.gsa_km2)) {
    stat("Model area", paste0("\u2248 ", fmt(sum(.gsa_km2[as.character(g)], na.rm = TRUE))), "from the map polygons; 01 computes the exact value")
  } else stat("Model area", "computed by 01", "these GSAs are not in the last run's model_area_cells.csv", warn = TRUE)
  uns <- intersect(g, .unsurveyed)
  fluidRow(
    stat("GSAs", length(g), paste(sort(g), collapse = ", ")),
    area_box,
    stat("Survey coverage", paste0(length(setdiff(g, .unsurveyed)), " of ", length(g)),
         if (length(uns)) paste0("GSA ", paste(uns, collapse = ", "), ": survey density assumed") else "all GSAs sampled by MEDITS",
         warn = length(uns) > 0),
    stat("Catch countries", length(unique(.gsa_state[as.character(g)])), paste(unique(.gsa_state[as.character(g)]), collapse = ", ")))
})

## --- Settings block: the exact code the Run button executes ---------------
config_code <- reactive({
  yr <- function(v) paste0(v[1], ":", v[2])
  tf <- function(x) if (isTRUE(x)) "TRUE" else "FALSE"
  common <- c(
    sprintf("YEAR_ECOPATH     <- %s   # Ecopath baseline", yr(input$ecopath_years)),
    sprintf("TS_YEARS         <- %s   # Ecosim biomass series", yr(input$ts_years)),
    sprintf("STRATA           <- %s", tf(input$strata)),
    sprintf("DROP_OUTLIERS    <- %s", tf(input$drop_outliers)),
    sprintf("NORMALIZE_TS     <- %s", tf(input$normalize_ts)))
  head <- c(sprintf("## WMed EwE pipeline settings - from medbs_pipeline_methodology.qmd, %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")),
            "## Run from the scripts/ folder of the repo (paths come from config.R).",
            "CLEAN_START      <- FALSE   # keep the settings below")
  if (identical(input$area_mode, "custom")) {
    c(head,
      "AREA_MODE        <- \"custom\"",
      sprintf("AREA_NAME        <- \"%s\"", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", input$area_name)),
      sprintf("CUSTOM_BBOX      <- c(xmin = %s, xmax = %s, ymin = %s, ymax = %s)",
              input$bbox_xmin, input$bbox_xmax, input$bbox_ymin, input$bbox_ymax),
      common,
      "source(\"01_biomass.R\")   # a custom box runs the biomass script only")
  } else {
    c(head,
      sprintf("RUN_STEPS        <- %s", input$steps),
      sprintf("MODEL_GSAS       <- c(%s)", paste(sort(as.numeric(input$gsas)), collapse = ", ")),
      sprintf("MODEL_AREA_BASIS <- \"%s\"", input$basis),
      common,
      sprintf("START_YEAR       <- %d   # catch / effort series", input$catch_years[1]),
      sprintf("END_YEAR         <- %d", input$catch_years[2]),
      "source(\"run_pipeline_demo.R\")")
  }
})
output$config_text <- renderText(paste(config_code(), collapse = "\n"))
output$dl_config <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() if (identical(input$area_mode, "custom")) "wmed_custom_settings.R" else "wmed_pipeline_settings.R",
  content = function(file) writeLines(config_code(), file))

## --- Run -------------------------------------------------------------------
run_state <- reactiveVal("idle")          # idle | running | done | error
run_started <- reactiveVal(NULL)
run_finished <- reactiveVal(NULL)
run_steps <- reactiveVal(1:5)
step_seen <- reactiveVal(list())          # step number -> time its start line was first seen
last_finished <- reactiveVal(Sys.time())  # changes after every run -> images reload
run_note <- reactiveVal("")

.pid_alive <- function() {
  pid <- if (file.exists(.pid_file)) suppressWarnings(as.integer(readLines(.pid_file, warn = FALSE)[1])) else NA
  !is.na(pid) && isTRUE(tryCatch(tools::pskill(pid, 0L), error = function(e) FALSE))
}
.settings_lines <- function() if (file.exists(.settings_file)) readLines(.settings_file, warn = FALSE) else character(0)

## Reopened page: pick up the last run started from here (finished, failed,
## or still going)
if (file.exists(.settings_file)) {
  run_started(file.mtime(.settings_file))
  .st <- grep("^RUN_STEPS", .settings_lines(), value = TRUE)
  run_steps(tryCatch(eval(parse(text = sub("^[^<]*<-", "", .st[1]))), error = function(e) 1:5))
  if (file.exists(.status_file)) {
    run_state(if (identical(readLines(.status_file, warn = FALSE)[1], "done")) "done" else "error")
    run_finished(file.mtime(.status_file))
  } else if (.pid_alive()) {
    run_state("running")
  } else {
    run_state("error"); run_finished(file.mtime(.console))
    run_note("The last run from this page stopped without finishing (R or RStudio was closed?).")
  }
}

observe({   # the Run button is for GSA runs only (disabled= needs shiny >= 1.11)
  lab <- if (identical(run_state(), "running")) "Running..." else if (identical(input$area_mode, "custom")) "Run (GSA mode only)" else "Run pipeline"
  if (utils::packageVersion("shiny") >= "1.11.0")
    updateActionButton(session, "run", label = lab,
                       disabled = identical(input$area_mode, "custom") || identical(run_state(), "running")) else
    updateActionButton(session, "run", label = lab)
})

observeEvent(input$run, {
  if (identical(run_state(), "running") || identical(input$area_mode, "custom")) return()
  if (!length(input$gsas)) { showNotification("Select at least one GSA.", type = "error"); return() }
  unlink(c(.status_file, .progress_file, .console, .pid_file))
  writeLines(config_code(), .settings_file)
  Sys.setenv(WMED_PROGRESS_FILE = .progress_file)   # inherited by the Rscript process
  ## The settings block, with the final source() wrapped so the result is reported back here
  body <- config_code()
  body <- body[!grepl("^##", body)]
  code <- paste(c(sprintf("writeLines(as.character(Sys.getpid()), '%s')", .pid_file), sub("^source\\(\"run_pipeline_demo.R\"\\)$",
                      "res <- tryCatch({ source('run_pipeline_demo.R'); 'done' }, error = function(e) paste('error:', conditionMessage(e)))", body),
                  sprintf("writeLines(res, '%s')", .status_file)), collapse = "\n")
  old <- setwd(file.path(.git_dir, "scripts")); on.exit(setwd(old))
  system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c("-e", shQuote(code)), wait = FALSE, stdout = .console, stderr = .console)
  run_state("running"); run_started(Sys.time()); run_finished(NULL); run_note(""); step_seen(list())
  run_steps(eval(parse(text = input$steps)))
  showNotification("Pipeline started - progress is shown below the button.", duration = 8)
})

## Poll the status file while a run is going
observe({
  if (!identical(run_state(), "running")) return()
  invalidateLater(5000)
  if (file.exists(.status_file)) {
    res <- readLines(.status_file, warn = FALSE)[1]
    run_state(if (identical(res, "done")) "done" else "error")
    run_finished(file.mtime(.status_file)); last_finished(Sys.time())
    showNotification(if (identical(res, "done")) "Pipeline finished - plots updated." else res,
                     type = if (identical(res, "done")) "message" else "error", duration = NULL)
  } else if (file.exists(.pid_file) && !.pid_alive()) {
    run_state("error"); run_finished(Sys.time()); last_finished(Sys.time())
    run_note("The run stopped without finishing - see the last lines below.")
  }
})

## Progress: read the "--- Step i/5: ..." / "--- Step i/5 done in x min ---"
## lines that run_pipeline_demo.R writes, and estimate the share done from
## the expected minutes per script.
output$run_progress <- renderUI({
  invalidateLater(3000)
  st <- run_state()
  if (identical(st, "idle")) {
    steps <- eval(parse(text = input$steps))
    return(tags$small(class = "text-muted", sprintf("Expected run time about %.0f min (%s).", sum(.step_min[steps]),
                                                   paste(.step_names[steps], collapse = ", "))))
  }
  lines <- if (file.exists(.progress_file)) readLines(.progress_file, warn = FALSE) else character(0)
  started <- as.integer(sub("^--- Step (\\d)/5:.*", "\\1", grep("^--- Step \\d/5: ", lines, value = TRUE)))
  finished <- as.integer(sub("^--- Step (\\d)/5 done.*", "\\1", grep("^--- Step \\d/5 done", lines, value = TRUE)))
  seen <- isolate(step_seen())
  for (k in setdiff(started, as.integer(names(seen)))) seen[[as.character(k)]] <- Sys.time()
  isolate(step_seen(seen))
  steps <- run_steps(); w <- .step_min[steps]
  current <- setdiff(started, finished); current <- if (length(current)) max(current) else NA
  done_min <- sum(.step_min[intersect(finished, steps)])
  cur_min <- if (!is.na(current)) min(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), seen[[as.character(current)]], units = "mins")),
                                      0.95 * .step_min[current]) else 0
  pct <- if (st == "done") 100 else round(100 * (done_min + cur_min) / sum(w))
  elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(if (is.null(run_finished())) Sys.time() else run_finished(), run_started(), units = "mins"))
  label <- switch(st,
    running = paste0(if (!is.na(current)) paste0("Running ", .step_names[current]) else "Starting",
                     " - ", length(intersect(finished, steps)), " of ", length(steps), " script(s) done - ",
                     sprintf("%.1f", elapsed), " min elapsed, about ", sprintf("%.0f", max(sum(w) - done_min - cur_min, 0)), " min left"),
    done = sprintf("Finished %s, in %.1f min", format(run_finished(), "%d %b %H:%M"), elapsed),
    error = "Stopped with an error - see below")
  colour <- switch(st, running = "bg-info", done = "bg-success", error = "bg-danger")
  ## one chip per script: done / running / waiting
  chips <- lapply(steps, function(k) {
    cls <- if (k %in% finished || st == "done") "bg-success" else if (identical(k, current)) "bg-info" else "bg-light text-dark"
    tags$span(class = paste("badge rounded-pill me-1", cls), .step_names[k])
  })
  tagList(
    tags$div(class = "progress mb-1", style = "height: 22px; border-radius: 11px;",
             tags$div(class = paste("progress-bar progress-bar-striped", colour, if (st == "running") "progress-bar-animated"),
                      role = "progressbar", style = paste0("width: ", pct, "%;"), paste0(pct, "%"))),
    tags$div(class = "mb-1", chips),
    tags$small(label))
})

output$run_status <- renderText({
  invalidateLater(5000)
  st <- run_state()
  tail_txt <- if (file.exists(.console)) paste(tail(readLines(.console, warn = FALSE), 3), collapse = "\n") else ""
  paste0("Status: ", st, "\nOutput folder: ", .out_dir,
         if (st == "error" && file.exists(.status_file)) paste0("\n", readLines(.status_file, warn = FALSE)[1]) else "",
         if (nzchar(run_note())) paste0("\n", run_note()) else "",
         if (nzchar(tail_txt)) paste0("\n--- last lines ---\n", tail_txt) else "")
})

## --- Results: key plots and every plot in out_dir/plots ----------------------
## The PNGs are served straight from out_dir/plots (no copy); "?v=<time>"
## makes the browser fetch a plot again after a run rewrites it.
.plot_dir <- if (!is.na(.out_dir)) file.path(.out_dir, "plots") else NA_character_
if (!is.na(.plot_dir) && dir.exists(.plot_dir)) addResourcePath("wmplots", .plot_dir)
.key_plots <- c("Biomass by source" = "biomass/biomass_by_fg_source.png",
                "Biomass series"    = "biomass/survey_fg_density_timeseries_regional.png",
                "Catch by FG"       = "fisheries/01_catches_per_FG.png",
                "F by FG"           = "validation/F_by_fg.png",
                "P/Q by FG"         = "validation/PQ_ratio_by_fg.png",
                "Diet matrix"       = "diets/diet_matrix_heatmap.png",
                "vs 1995 model"     = "validation/biomass_vs_old_model_by_fg.png")

output$results <- renderUI({
  last_finished(); st <- run_state()
  files <- if (!is.na(.plot_dir)) list.files(.plot_dir, "\\.png$", recursive = TRUE) else character(0)
  if (!length(files)) return(tags$div(class = "alert alert-secondary py-2 small mb-0", "No plots yet - click Run pipeline."))
  mt <- file.mtime(file.path(.plot_dir, files)); names(mt) <- files
  src <- function(f) paste0("wmplots/", utils::URLencode(f), "?v=", as.integer(mt[[f]]))
  fmt <- function(t) format(t, "%d %b %Y, %H:%M")

  ## Where these plots come from
  newest <- max(mt)
  set <- .settings_lines()
  set <- gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(sub("#.*", "", set[grepl("^(MODEL_GSAS|MODEL_AREA_BASIS|YEAR_ECOPATH|TS_YEARS|START_YEAR|END_YEAR|DROP_OUTLIERS)", set)])))
  from_here <- !is.null(run_finished()) && !is.null(run_started()) &&
               newest >= run_started() && newest <= run_finished() + 120
  banner <- if (identical(st, "running")) {
    tags$div(class = "alert alert-warning py-2 small", "A run is going. These are the previous plots; they are replaced when it finishes.")
  } else if (from_here && identical(st, "done")) {
    tags$div(class = "alert alert-success py-2 small",
             tags$strong("From the run started on this page "), sprintf("on %s, finished %s. ", fmt(run_started()), fmt(run_finished())),
             tags$br(), tags$code(paste(set, collapse = "; ")))
  } else {
    tags$div(class = "alert alert-info py-2 small",
             sprintf("Plots last written %s by a run outside this page (from the R console or another session).", fmt(newest)),
             if (!is.null(run_started())) sprintf(" The last run from this page was on %s.", fmt(run_started())))
  }

  ## Key plots: one tab each
  ids <- paste0("wm-key-", seq_along(.key_plots))
  key_nav <- tags$ul(class = "nav nav-tabs", role = "tablist",
    lapply(seq_along(.key_plots), function(i)
      tags$li(class = "nav-item", role = "presentation",
              tags$button(class = paste("nav-link", if (i == 1) "active"), type = "button", role = "tab",
                          `data-bs-toggle` = "tab", `data-bs-target` = paste0("#", ids[i]), names(.key_plots)[i]))))
  key_body <- tags$div(class = "tab-content",
    lapply(seq_along(.key_plots), function(i) {
      f <- .key_plots[[i]]
      tags$div(class = paste("tab-pane fade", if (i == 1) "show active"), id = ids[i], role = "tabpanel",
               if (f %in% files) tags$img(class = "wm-key-img", src = src(f), alt = basename(f))
               else tags$div(class = "alert alert-secondary small mt-2", "Not available yet: plots/", f))
    }))

  ## All plots: thumbnails, filter by folder, search by name
  folder <- dirname(files)
  ord <- order(folder, basename(files)); files <- files[ord]; folder <- folder[ord]
  counts <- table(folder)
  filt <- tags$div(class = "wm-filter",
    tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary active", `data-folder` = "", sprintf("All (%d)", length(files))),
    lapply(names(counts), function(d)
      tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary", `data-folder` = d, sprintf("%s (%d)", d, counts[[d]]))),
    tags$input(id = "wm-search", type = "search", class = "form-control form-control-sm", placeholder = "Search plot name"))
  grid <- tags$div(class = "wm-grid",
    lapply(seq_along(files), function(i)
      tags$div(class = "wm-thumb", `data-folder` = folder[i], `data-name` = tolower(basename(files[i])),
               tags$img(src = src(files[i]), loading = "lazy", alt = basename(files[i]), title = "Click to zoom"),
               tags$div(class = "wm-thumb-folder", folder[i]),
               tags$div(class = "wm-thumb-name", sub("\\.png$", "", basename(files[i]))))))

  tagList(
    banner,
    tags$ul(class = "nav nav-pills wm-view", role = "tablist",
      tags$li(class = "nav-item", tags$button(class = "nav-link active", type = "button", `data-bs-toggle` = "pill",
                                              `data-bs-target` = "#wm-view-key", "Key plots")),
      tags$li(class = "nav-item", tags$button(class = "nav-link", type = "button", `data-bs-toggle` = "pill",
                                              `data-bs-target` = "#wm-view-all", sprintf("All plots (%d)", length(files))))),
    tags$div(class = "tab-content",
      tags$div(class = "tab-pane fade show active", id = "wm-view-key", key_nav, key_body),
      tags$div(class = "tab-pane fade", id = "wm-view-all", filt, grid)),
    tags$small(class = "text-muted", "Click any plot to zoom. Plots are read from ", tags$code(.plot_dir), "."))
})
```

| Input | Script variable | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| GSAs (map, checkboxes) | `MODEL_GSAS` (→ `FILTER_AREAS`) | GSAs of the model area. Survey data only from these GSAs; GSAs 3 and 4 (no MEDITS) take the survey density per km² of the others (assumption). Catch kept for every coastal state of these GSAs. |
| Area basis | `MODEL_AREA_BASIS` | `whole_gsa`: A_model is the whole sea area of the GSAs, coast to bottom. `medits_10_800`: only the 10-800 m MEDITS strata. |
| Custom box | `AREA_MODE = "custom"`, `AREA_NAME`, `CUSTOM_BBOX` | A rectangular region instead of GSAs (01_biomass.R only, @sec-area-definition Approach B). |
| Ecopath baseline | `YEAR_ECOPATH` | Years averaged into Ecopath_B, F and P/B (01, 02, 03). |
| Ecosim biomass series | `TS_YEARS` | Years of the Ecosim biomass series (01). |
| Catch and effort series | `START_YEAR`, `END_YEAR` | Years of the catch, landings, discards and effort series (02). |
| Strata-weighted density | `STRATA` (default `TRUE`) | Depth-stratum, area-weighted estimator (@sec-strata-weighted) vs a simple mean. |
| Remove outliers | `DROP_OUTLIERS` (default `TRUE`) | Flagged outlier hauls removed, or only reported in `survey_outliers_flagged.csv`. |
| Relative Ecosim series | `NORMALIZE_TS` (default `TRUE`) | Ecosim series as an index (first value = 1) or raw density. |
| Scripts to run | `RUN_STEPS` | `1:5` all; `2:5` reuses the biomass on disk; `5` redraws the validation only. |

The model-area figure in the summary is a preview from the simplified map polygons (about 1 % above the real value); the A_model used in the outputs is the one 01 computes and writes to `model_area_by_gsa.csv`.

## Overview

This document explains the methodology behind `lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R`, a generalized function library for converting fishery-independent survey data (biomass/density by species, haul, year, area, stratum) into a Functional Group (FG) density index suitable as Ecopath/Ecosim input.

**What this produces and why it matters:** the output of this stage is a time series of biomass density per Functional Group — how much of each modeled group is really out there, year by year, for whichever region and time window is configured. Everything else in the wider pipeline (catches, mortality, production, diet) is expressed relative to this density, so getting it right — correctly weighted by survey stratum and area, not just averaged naively — is what lets the rest of the model be trusted.

Unlike the original, MEDITS-specific `medbs_full_pipeline_with_fg.R` script this document previously covered, the pipeline is now split into two layers:

1. **A shared, survey-agnostic function library** (`lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R`) - the statistical logic (strata weighting, area weighting, outlier detection, catchability correction) that doesn't depend on which survey or which study area boundary is being used.
2. **One Step-1 driver script, `01_biomass.R`,** that reads the survey's raw files, reshapes them into the library's standardized input format and calls the shared functions. `AREA_MODE` picks the study area:
   - `AREA_MODE = "westmed"` (default) - MEDITS bottom-trawl data, study area defined by the official GFCM GSA polygons (`MODEL_GSAS`, set in `run_pipeline_demo.R` with the years; default GSAs 1–11, the whole Western Med; MEDITS/MEDIAS data exist for GSAs 1, 2, 5–11). Also incorporates MEDIAS acoustic survey data (@sec-medias), combined with MEDITS into a single density index, and sources `01b_biomass_unsurveyed.R` for the groups the surveys cannot measure (@sec-biomass). Outputs in `out_dir/biomass/` and `out_dir/plots/biomass/`.
   - `AREA_MODE = "custom"` - the same MEDITS data with a custom boundary (bounding box, any shapefile, or a custom GSA grouping; `CUSTOM_AREA_TYPE`) - useful when the same survey supports a different EwE model with its own footprint. MEDITS-only. Outputs in `out_dir/<AREA_NAME>/` (default `custom_region`), so the two modes never overwrite each other.

(The former separate scripts `01_survey_density_westmed.R` and `01_survey_density_custom.R` are retired; their logic lives in `01_biomass.R`.)

Code chunks throughout are **not executed** when this document renders (`eval: false`) - they're shown for reference alongside the explanation, since the pipeline depends on external data files and network access (bathymetry downloads, WoRMS taxonomy lookups) not available at render time. Run the source `.R` scripts directly to reproduce the actual numbers. (The exceptions are the figure-copying setup chunk above and the `safe_include_graphics()` calls below, which only need the plot files to exist on disk, degrading to a placeholder message rather than failing the render if a given example script hasn't been run yet.)

The pipeline covers several conceptually distinct problems in sequence:

1. **Which Functional Group does each species belong to?** (@sec-fg-matching)
2. **What study area am I actually working with?** (@sec-area-definition)
3. **Given catch and effort, what's the correctly-standardized density for each haul?** (@sec-density, including catchability correction and outlier removal)
4. **Given that, what's the correctly-weighted density estimate for each FG?** (@sec-strata-weighted, @sec-regional)
5. **For the westmed script specifically: how does a second, structurally different survey (acoustic, not trawl) get folded into the same index?** (@sec-medias)

### Pipeline flow

```{mermaid}

%%| eval: true

flowchart LR
    A1["Direct match (ScientificName lookup)"] --> A2["Nominate subspp. (repeated-word names)"]
    A2 --> A3["Taxonomy fallback (genus to phylum)"]

```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-flow-density-weighting
%%| fig-cap: "Density and weighting detail (@sec-density, @sec-strata-weighted, @sec-regional) - dashed boxes are conditional steps, skipped if their condition isn't met."
%%| eval: true
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'padding': 20, 'nodeSpacing': 60, 'rankSpacing': 90}, 'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '20px'}}}%%
flowchart LR
    B1["Sample density (biomass / effort)"] --> B2(["Catchability (if q table given)"])
    B2 --> B3["Outlier removal (per species, per area)"]
    B3 --> B4(["Strata weighting (if strata = true)"])
    B4 --> B5(["Area weighting (if more than one area)"])

    classDef teal fill:#E1F5EE,stroke:#0F6E56,color:#04342C
    class B1,B3 teal
    class B2,B4,B5 teal
```

Dashed/rounded boxes above are conditional: catchability correction only runs if a catchability table is provided, strata weighting only if `strata = TRUE` (otherwise a simple mean density is used instead), and area weighting is only meaningful with more than one area in scope (with a single custom region, it still runs but is mathematically a formality - see @sec-regional).

Problems 3 and 4 are the most statistically subtle - a naive average across hauls, or treating every survey estimate as if the gear caught 100% of what was present, can be quietly wrong in ways that matter for the final model.

## Input files {#sec-inputs}

Every file the pipeline actually reads, traced directly from `01_biomass.R` (both `AREA_MODE`s)'s own variable assignments - not a general description, the literal paths and variable names used in the code.

| File | Variable | Used for | Required? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FG_WMed_2026.csv` | `fg_file` | Species→FG reference master (`dataframe2`, @sec-fg-matching) | Yes, both scripts |
| `TM_list_(April_2019).xlsx` | `tm_list_file` | MEDITS species code → `ScientificName` lookup | Yes, both scripts |
| `TA.csv` | loaded as `ta` | MEDITS haul-level metadata - station, depth, swept area, effort | Yes, both scripts |
| `TB.csv` | loaded as `tb` | MEDITS catch-per-haul records | Yes, both scripts |
| `ASFIS_sp_2026.1.csv` | `asfis_file` | FAO species code list - MEDIAS species code → `ScientificName` (@sec-medias) | westmed only |
| `abundance.csv` / `biomass.csv` | in `medias_dir` | MEDIAS acoustic survey raw records (@sec-medias) | westmed only |
| `catchability_factors_ecotrans_medits_2021_spp.csv` | `CATCHABILITY_CSV_PATH` | Optional per-species catchability correction factors (@sec-density) | Optional - falls back to `q = 1` (no correction) if missing |
| GFCM GSA shapefile (`GFCM_GSA.zip`) | downloaded to `area_shp` | Official GSA boundary polygons (@sec-area-definition, Approach A) | westmed only - downloaded automatically, not a local file |
| NOAA bathymetry raster | downloaded via `marmap::getNOAA.bathy()` | Stratum area computation (@sec-strata-weighted) | Both scripts - downloaded automatically |
| Custom shapefile / bounding box | `CUSTOM_BBOX` or a user-supplied shapefile path | Study area definition (@sec-area-definition, Approach B) | custom script only |

::: {.callout-important}
### Note: `fg_file` is the current CSV, not the retired xlsx
`fg_file` is `FG_WMed_2026.csv` (a flat, reviewed CSV - species/FG_number/FG_name/Genus/Family/Order/Class/Phylum), not `FG_WMed.xlsx`. The old `FG_WMed.xlsx` workbook (sheet 4 for the species→FG master, plus its own `traits_ewe` sheet) is retired - `01_biomass.R`/`02_fisheries.R`/`03_pbqb-traits.R`/`04_diets.R` all read `FG_WMed_2026.csv` directly via `fread()`, never `readxl::read_excel()`. The `traits_ewe` **sheet**-parsing mechanism described in the callout below (@sec-configure) is correspondingly retired too - `03_pbqb-traits.R` now builds `traits_ewe` from FishBase/SeaLifeBase life-history data instead of parsing an xlsx sheet; see @sec-pbqb-traits below for the current method.
:::

All the pCloud-hosted files above share one root, `pcloud_dir` (@sec-configure resolves this the same portable way it resolves `git_dir` - hardcoded on your machine, an interactive picker for anyone else) - so moving or renaming the `Medits_Medias_JRC2026` folder structure itself would break every path in the table above, not just one.

::: {.callout-note}
### Two downloads happen automatically - no local file needed
The GSA shapefile and the bathymetry raster aren't files you provide - both are fetched over the network the first time a script needs them (from GFCM's own Azure blob storage, and from NOAA respectively) and cached locally afterward (`gsa_shp_dir`/`GFCM_GSA_shp` for the shapefile; wherever `getNOAA.bathy()`'s own cache lands, keyed by the bounding box requested) so re-running the script doesn't re-download every time. This is also why `eval: false` on the code chunks throughout this document matters (@sec-configure) - reproducing this pipeline's actual output needs live network access at least once, which isn't guaranteed at render time.
:::

```{r}
#| label: bathymetry-download
#| code-fold: false
## Real call, from lib_survey_fg_density_functions.R's strata-area
## computation (@sec-strata-weighted) - bbox comes from the study
## area's own extent (a GSA polygon or the custom region), so this
## downloads only the bathymetry actually needed, not the whole
## Mediterranean every time.
bathy <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(lon1 = bbox["xmin"], lon2 = bbox["xmax"],
                                lat1 = bbox["ymin"], lat2 = bbox["ymax"],
                                resolution = 1, keep = TRUE)
bathy_r <- marmap::as.raster(bathy)
```

## Functional Group matching {#sec-fg-matching}

Every species caught in a haul needs to be assigned to one of the model's Functional Groups before its biomass can contribute to an FG-level index. This happens in stages, each one only attempting species the previous stage couldn't resolve - and at every stage, an **ambiguous** match (a species or taxonomic rank that could plausibly belong to more than one FG) is flagged for manual review rather than guessed.

### Stage 1 - Direct species-level match

The MEDITS species code is translated to a scientific name via the MEDITS taxonomic list (`TM_list`), then matched directly against the FG reference table.

```{r}
#| label: direct-match
fg_lookup_safe <- prepare_fg_lookup(dataframe2)
dt <- match_species_to_fg(dataframe1, fg_lookup_safe)
```

`prepare_fg_lookup()` also resolves **stanza splits** here - a species appearing in more than one FG, where every one of those FGs is exclusive to that single species (a life-stage split, e.g. juvenile/adult), is reduced to one FG automatically. This is a structural rule (detected from the FG table's own shape), not a text-pattern match on words like "juv." - so it works regardless of the wording convention any given FG scheme happens to use. A species spanning multiple FGs where at least one of those FGs also contains *other* species is a genuinely different, ambiguous case and is excluded from automatic matching entirely.

### Stage 1b - Nominate subspecies

Some scientific names are trinomials for the nominate subspecies, where the subspecies epithet repeats the species epithet by taxonomic convention (e.g. "Diplodus sargus sargus" is the nominate subspecies of "Diplodus sargus"). These fail a direct match if the FG reference only has the binomial form.

```{r}
#| label: nominate-subspecies
dt <- match_nominate_subspecies_fg(dt, fg_lookup_safe)
```

### Stage 2 - Manual overrides

A short table of species codes not present in the MEDITS taxonomic list at all, resolved by hand at whichever taxonomic rank is appropriate (species, genus, family, or class). Merged on `species_code`, not `ScientificName` - the latter is exactly the column that's `NA` for override-needed rows (that's *why* they need an override), so using it as a join key would match every `NA` row against every other `NA` row and produce a cartesian-product explosion.

### Stage 3 - Taxonomy fallback (genus through phylum)

For species with a resolved scientific name but no FG match, WoRMS taxonomy is used to check progressively broader ranks - genus, family, order, class, phylum, most specific first.

```{r}
#| label: taxonomy-fallback
dt <- fallback_match_fg_by_taxonomy(dt, fg_lookup_safe, taxonomy_source = "worms")
```

**Safety rule**, applied at every rank: a taxonomic value is only used for fallback matching if it maps to **exactly one** FG among all species already in the reference table.

$$\text{rank value is safe to use} \iff \left| \{\, FG_i : \text{species}_i \text{ shares this rank value} \,\} \right| = 1$$

A genus spanning multiple FGs (e.g. containing both a small pelagic species and a large predatory one) is too ecologically diverse to assign safely, and is excluded rather than assigned to whichever FG happens to come up first. Ranks are tried in order of specificity - a genus-level match always wins over a broader but explicit order-level rule for the same species, since rank specificity takes priority over whether a mapping happened to be data-driven or explicitly stated.

### Stage 4 - Seed rules for catch-all FGs

Some FGs (e.g. "Other macro-benthos") have **zero species pre-listed** against them in the FG reference table - they're buckets meant to catch "anything else" of a general taxonomic type. The data-driven fallback above can't discover a mapping for these, since it can only learn from species already assigned to an FG. A small, explicit seed table covers this genuine gap:

```{r}
#| label: seed-rules
SEED_RULES <- data.table(
  rank = c("Class", "Order", "Phylum"),
  rank_value = c("Holothuroidea", "Decapoda", "Cnidaria"),
  fg_name_target = c("Sea cucumbers", "Non-commercial decapods", "Other macro-benthos")
)
SPECIES_EXCEPTIONS <- data.table(
  ScientificName = "Squilla mantis",
  fg_name_target = "Other commercial decapods"
)
dt <- apply_seed_fg_rules(dt, dataframe2, SEED_RULES, species_exceptions = SPECIES_EXCEPTIONS)
```

`species_exceptions` is applied *before* the rank-based rules, so a named species is never caught by a broader rule that's wrong for it specifically - e.g. Squilla mantis is commercially exploited even though the rest of its order (Stomatopoda) isn't, so the generic "Decapoda-adjacent → non-commercial" rule would misclassify it without this override.

### Match-rate reporting

```{r}
#| label: match-rate-reporting
taxonomy_context <- attr(dt, "still_unresolved_taxonomy")
still_unmatched <- summarize_unresolved_species(dt, taxonomy = taxonomy_context)
```

`summarize_unresolved_species()` reports mean biomass and appearance count alongside taxonomy for whatever remains genuinely unmatched, so manual review can be prioritized - a species appearing in hundreds of samples with real biomass matters more than a one-off trace appearance.

---

## Study area definition {#sec-area-definition}

Every function downstream of FG matching needs to know which "area" each sample belongs to, and needs a polygon layer to compute stratum areas from bathymetry. The shared library doesn't assume this has to be a set of official GSA polygons - it just needs *some* polygon layer with an ID column. Two approaches are covered here.

### Approach A - GFCM GSA polygons

The official GFCM GSA shapefile is downloaded once and cached. MEDITS' own `area` field already gives each haul's GSA directly, so no spatial join is needed.

```{r}
#| label: gsa-area-setup
gsa_shp_path <- list.files(gsa_shp_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)[1]
area_shp <- st_read(gsa_shp_path, quiet = TRUE)
area_shp$gsa_num <- as.numeric(area_shp$SMU_CODE)
area_shp$gsa_num[area_shp$gsa_num %in% c(111, 112)] <- 11   # Western/Eastern Sardinia -> single GSA 11
AREA_ID_COL <- "gsa_num"
FILTER_AREAS <- 1:11
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-gsa-coverage
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Sample coverage by GSA. selected_areas highlights the GSAs actually in scope (FILTER_AREAS) with a bold black outline - the outer contour of their union, not the internal lines between them."
#| out-width: "100%"
safe_include_graphics(file.path("figures", "survey_sample_coverage_map.png"), "01_biomass.R (AREA_MODE = \"westmed\")")
```

### Approach B - a custom boundary (bounding box or arbitrary shapefile)

The same MEDITS raw data can instead be restricted to a custom footprint that doesn't correspond to any GSA code - a simple bounding box, or a shapefile for a different EwE model's own boundary.

```{r}
#| label: custom-area-setup
CUSTOM_BBOX <- c(xmin = 2, xmax = 8, ymin = 38, ymax = 42)
custom_poly <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(
  xmin = unname(CUSTOM_BBOX["xmin"]), ymin = unname(CUSTOM_BBOX["ymin"]),
  xmax = unname(CUSTOM_BBOX["xmax"]), ymax = unname(CUSTOM_BBOX["ymax"])
), crs = 4326))
area_shp <- st_sf(area_id = 1, geometry = custom_poly)
AREA_ID_COL <- "area_id"

dataframe1 <- filter_samples_by_area(dataframe1, area_filter = CUSTOM_BBOX, filter_type = "bbox")
dataframe1[, AreaID := 1]
```

::: {.callout-note}
### `unname()` matters here
`CUSTOM_BBOX["xmin"]` carries the name `"xmin"` with it (it's already a named vector element) - `c(xmin = CUSTOM_BBOX["xmin"], ...)` without `unname()` concatenates into `"xmin.xmin"` instead of `"xmin"`, which `st_bbox()` can't parse. This is the same bug class that shows up anywhere a named-vector element gets re-wrapped in another named vector - it also affected an earlier version of the land-basemap layer in `plot_sample_map()`, for the same reason.
:::

`filter_samples_by_area(filter_type = "shapefile")` works the same way, but takes an `sf` polygon (or a path to one) instead of a bounding box - for a real, non-rectangular model boundary.

::: {.callout-note}
### The sample coverage map shows the full survey context, not just the custom box
`plot_sample_map()` computes its display extent from the **union** of `area_shp`'s own bounding box and the sample points' own Lat/Lon distribution - not `area_shp`'s bbox alone. Passing it the full, unfiltered survey data (before `filter_samples_by_area()` runs) means the map zooms out to show the complete MEDITS distribution across the whole survey region, with the custom area's contour highlighted within that context via `selected_areas` - not a tight, context-free zoom into just the small box itself. Points inside vs. outside the selected area are shown in different colors either way.

A plain bounding box, unlike the GFCM GSA polygons, is not coastline-aware - it can genuinely overlap land. `land_on_top = TRUE` draws the land basemap *after* the intensity fill rather than before, so any part of the box that's actually land is visibly masked - only marine area should read as part of the study region, and a rectangle has no way to exclude land on its own.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-custom-coverage
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Sample coverage within a custom bounding-box region, independent of GSA lines entirely."
#| out-width: "100%"
safe_include_graphics(file.path("figures", "custom_survey_sample_coverage_map.png"), "01_biomass.R (AREA_MODE = \"custom\")")
```

With only one custom area, `AreaID` is set to `1` for every retained sample - there's no sub-division unless the boundary is itself split into multiple named sub-zones. Every function further downstream (strata weighting, area weighting, Excel export) works identically either way; they only ever see whatever `AreaID`/`area_shp` combination they're given, never assuming GSA-specific structure.
